title: Five follow-ups to the Chrome APIs plan
blurb: One stage, five small experiments: tiles that swap to a one-sentence stand-in when they are too small to read, the columns of a multi-column element turned like pages, canvas text selection rectangles against DOM range rectangles, a float WebGL buffer with a bloom pass, and a shader effect picked by a custom property.
question: What do five open ideas from the Chrome APIs plan do when built: semantic zoom, column pages, TextMetrics selection rectangles, a float WebGL buffer, and an effect chosen in CSS?
result: All five draw. A multi-column element is one picture that holds every column. Scroll markers of a column scroller are not in the picture. TextMetrics.getSelectionRects() needs Chrome 160 or the experimental flag. A drawable WebGL canvas accepts an RGBA16F drawing buffer. A registered custom-ident changes at the halfway point of a transition.
